provenance: Synthetic, single-author challenge items created before V9 implementation. No external or independent reviewers; not real-world accuracy evidence.
annotationAudit: None yet. Any post-scoring label correction will be disclosed here without changing texts or split membership.

items.text: I'm going to choke you if you come closer.
items.targetingEvidence: First-person future intent with a second-person human object.
items.rationale: An explicit stated intent to choke a person is a direct threat; the verb is absent from the current closed injury-verb list.

items.targetingEvidence: First-person future intent, possessive human body part, and an injury result.
items.rationale: A body-part injury construction with a human object; the object/result vocabulary is currently uncovered.

items.targetingEvidence: First-person future intent with a third-person human body-part object.
items.rationale: The general body-part rule covers jaw/nose but not face; a human possessive object distinguishes this from breaking a thing.

items.targetingEvidence: First-person future verb with a second-person object suffix.
items.rationale: A direct Egyptian Arabic threat of physical injury absent from the attested verb list.

items.targetingEvidence: First-person future verb with a third-person feminine object suffix.
items.rationale: The same injury act with a third-person object must be covered without a broader verb generalization.

items.text: I'm going to choke you لو قربت.
items.targetingEvidence: English future-intent injury clause with an Arabic condition.
items.rationale: Mixed-script feed text must not evade a covered English injury construction.

items.text: This update will knock your socks off.
items.targetingEvidence: Positive idiom with a clothing object, not a body-part injury.
items.rationale: Hard negative: the knock-construction must require teeth/head, not any possessive object.

items.text: I'll choke on my coffee if I eat too fast.
items.targetingEvidence: The speaker is the one who may choke; no human object is targeted.
items.rationale: Hard negative: choke must require a second/third-person human object.

items.text: We need to break the build before release.
items.targetingEvidence: The object is a build artifact.
items.rationale: Hard negative: injury verbs must not generalize to non-human objects.

items.text: I'm going to break your fall with this cushion.
items.targetingEvidence: Possessive object is an event, not a body part.
items.rationale: Hard negative: a possessive pronoun alone is not injury evidence.

items.text: مش هخنقك، خلينا نحل المشكلة بالكلام.
items.targetingEvidence: Explicit negation of the injury verb with peaceful intent.
items.rationale: Hard negative: the new verb must be added to the attested negation suppression forms.

items.text: قال هخنقك لو رجعت للشارع ده.
items.targetingEvidence: The threat is attributed to another speaker by قال.
items.rationale: Reporting a threat must remain visible; the existing reporting cue must keep governing this sentence.

items.targetingEvidence: The object is a process, not a person; no object suffix is attached to the verb.
items.rationale: Hard negative: the Arabic verb alone must not match without a personal object suffix.

items.text: She said she would choke you.
items.targetingEvidence: Attributed speech with a conditional would, not author intent.
items.rationale: Hard negative: attribution and non-future modality must stay excluded.

items.text: I'm going to choke you for that joke 😂
items.targetingEvidence: The joke marker frames the injury wording as possible banter.
items.rationale: Isolated text cannot establish real intent; a documented false-positive risk rather than a clear negative.

items.text: هخنقك يا صاحبي في الماتش ده
items.targetingEvidence: The match frame makes friendly exaggeration plausible.
items.rationale: Ambiguous intent; excluded from metrics and not tuned away.
